title: Israeli Ad Firm Doubled as Candiru’s Zero-Click Spyware Delivery Channel
description: Discover-Tech, an Israeli advertising company, operated as a covert channel for Candiru spyware, enabling zero-click infections via malicious ads. These ads allowed threat actors to fingerprint, track, and de-anonymize millions of devices worldwide, including targeted attacks on Al Jazeera. The operation, named AdFection, exploited the online advertising ecosystem to deliver spyware without user interaction. Major platforms like Google and IAB Europe have removed Discover-Tech from their ad vendor registries and blocked its access to ad exchanges. Citizen Lab recommends blocking targeted ads at the gateway as the primary defense until industry-wide mitigations are effective.
aiSummary: Discover-Tech used its Controlium platform to serve ads embedded with malicious scripts that fingerprinted devices and executed zero-click spyware infections on behalf of Candiru, an Israeli spyware vendor. The ads collected advertising IDs and other identifiers to profile users and selectively infect targets. Citizen Lab's investigation revealed that Discover-Tech's ads appeared on nearly 200,000 websites and mobile applications globally, exposing billions of ad bid records. The campaign targeted at least 45 devices within Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025. The operation leveraged the real-time bidding ad ecosystem to deliver spyware infections at scale, effectively bridging ad vendors and mercenary spyware actors. Industry responses included removal from ad vendor registries and blocking by major ad platforms.
aiImpact: The campaign enabled large-scale de-anonymization, device fingerprinting, and zero-click spyware infections, compromising user privacy and security globally. Targeted organizations, such as Al Jazeera, suffered direct infections. The widespread presence of Discover-Tech ads across numerous websites and apps increased the risk of exposure to spyware infections. The operation facilitated persistent tracking and surveillance by threat actors, undermining user anonymity and security.
